(Fresno, California) | college = * [[Willamette Bearcats|Willamette]] (2021–2022) * [[Eastern Washington Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Washington]] (2022–2024) * [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 11 | draft_team = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] ({{nbay|2025|end}}) * First-team All-[[Big Sky Conference|Big Sky]] (2024) * [[Northwest Conference]] Freshman of the Year (2022) * First-team All-Northwest Conference (2022) }} '''Cedric De'Von Coward''' (born September 11, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Willamette Bearcats]], [[Eastern Washington Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Washington Eagles]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]]. ==Early life and high school career== Coward grew up in [[Fresno, California]] and attended [[Central High School (Fresno, California)|Central High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fresnobee.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/article281823568.html|title=Who were the top high school basketball players in the Fresno area? Here is our list|first=Anthony|last=Galaviz|work=[[The Fresno Bee]]|date=November 14, 2023|access-date=December 5, 2024}} ==College career== Coward began his college career at Division III [[Willamette University]]. In his only season with the Bearcats, averaged 19.5 points and 12.0 rebounds per game and was named the [[Northwest Conference]] Freshman of the Year and first-team All-Northwest.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/dec/19/eastern-washingtons-cedric-coward-carving-out-impo/|title=Eastern Washington's Cedric Coward carving out important role after transferring from Willamette|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=December 19, 2022|access-date=December 5, 2024}} After his freshman season, Coward transferred to [[Eastern Washington University]]. In his first season with the [[Eastern Washington Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Washington Eagles]], he averaged 7.3 points per game with 5.6 rebounds per game{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/washington-state/men-s-basketball/posts/new-washington-state-wing-cedric-coward-has-nba-potential|title=New Washington State Wing Cedric Coward Has NBA Potential|first=Keenan|last=Womack|website=[[SI.com]]|date=August 2, 2024|access-date=December 5, 2024}} Coward was named first-team All-[[Big Sky Conference]] as a junior after averaging 15.4 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/touted-cedric-coward-withdraws-from-nba-draft-is-wsu-next-stop-232239790/|title=Touted Cedric Coward withdraws from NBA Draft. Is WSU next stop?|first=Jamey|last=Vinnick|website=[[247Sports]]|date=May 27, 2024|access-date=December 5, 2024}} After the season, he entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/10/eastern-washington-standout-cedric-coward-enters-t/|title=Eastern Washington standout Cedric Coward enters transfer portal, to test NBA draft|first=Ralph|last=Walter|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=April 10, 2024|access-date=December 5, 2024}} Coward committed to transfer to [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/may/30/cedric-coward-commits-to-washington-state-becoming/|title=Cedric Coward commits to WSU, becoming fourth former EWU player to join coach David Riley|first=Greg|last=Woods|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=May 31, 2024|access-date=December 5, 2024}} He suffered a season-ending shoulder injury six games into his first season with the team.{{cite web|url=https://www.kxly.com/sports/after-successful-surgery-wsus-star-guard-cedric-coward-out-for-the-season-along-with-others/article_a85bfa36-ba7e-11ef-bae6-a3f1d338843f.html|title=After successful surgery, WSU's star guard Cedric Coward out for the season along with others|first=Sydney|last=Berger|website=[[KXLY-TV|KXLY.com]]|date=December 14, 2024|access-date=January 16, 2025}} At the time of his injury, Coward was the Cougars' leading scorer at 17.7 points per game and was averaging seven rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougars/wsu-tops-missouri-state-but-star-cedric-coward-ruled-out-for-season/|title=WSU tops Missouri State, but star Cedric Coward ruled out for season|first=Greg|last=Woods|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=December 14, 2024|access-date=January 16, 2025}} Following his senior season, Coward entered the transfer portal along with declaring for the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |title=Cedric Coward enters portal with "DNC" tag; LeJuan Watts quiet ... a return to Pullman possible? |url=https://247sports.com/article/cedric-coward-enters-transfer-portal-do-not-contact-tag-fifth-washington-state-player-in-portal-lejuan-watts-return-pullman-david-riley-248537170/ |access-date=May 24, 2025 |website=[[247Sports]] |language=en|date=April 10, 2025|last=Haugh|first=Dylan}} On April 28, 2025, he committed to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], but kept his name in the draft.{{Cite web |last=Baxley |first=Rodd |title=Duke basketball gets commitment from Cedric Coward, who could be starter for Blue Devils |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/acc/2025/04/28/cedric-coward-duke-basketball-transfer-portal-nba-draft/83333677007/ |access-date=May 24, 2025 |website=The Fayetteville Observer |language=en-US|date=April 28, 2025}} After the [[NBA draft combine|NBA Combine]], Coward announced on May 24 that he would forgo playing at Duke and remain in the draft pool.{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Andrew |title=Cedric Coward to Remain in 2025 NBA Draft After Committing to Duke in Transfer Portal |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25198983-cedric-coward-remain-2025-nba-draft-after-committing-duke-transfer-portal |access-date=May 24, 2025 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en|date=May 24, 2025}} ==Professional career== Coward was drafted 11th overall by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]] and subsequently traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for [[Yang Hansen]] and future draft considerations. He signed with the Grizzlies on July 8.{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2025 |title=Grizzlies sign Cedric Coward to Multi-Year Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-cedric-coward-to-multi-year-contract |access-date=July 20, 2025 |website=NBA.com}} On October 25, 2025, Coward put up 27 points on 6-for-6 shooting from three-point range in a 128–103 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He became the first rookie in Grizzlies franchise history to record at least six made three-pointers in a game without a miss.{{cite web|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/645870/rookie-cedric-coward-hits-all-6-3s-scores-27-in-grizzlies-win|title=Rookie Cedric Coward hits all 6 3s, scores 27 in Grizzlies win|website=Inquirer|date=October 26, 2025|access-date=October 30, 2025|agency=Associated Press}} At the end of his rookie season, Coward finished fifth in [[NBA Rookie of the Year|Rookie of the Year]] voting and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]]. ==Personal== Coward is the grandson of sprinter [[Maxie Parks]].{{Cite web |title=Q&A: Cedric Coward 'stayed believing' on his winding path to NBA |url=https://www.nba.com/news/qa-cedric-coward-memphis-grizzlies |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=NBA.com |language=en|date=November 28, 2025|last=Aschburner|first=Steve}} ==Career
